page.layout: One page of text: a continuation of the Latin couplets at the top, then a headed Psalm paraphrase in verse. Stanza numbers 1 to 3 and a short fragment stand in the right margin. A catchword stands at the lower right below the last line.

main_text.l: Profeßo[?] Deus est, iustos qui curat, & ampla Munera, syncera pro pietate refert.
Est etiam Numen, iusto quo uindice, iustas Iniustus pœnas impietatis habet.
Ne trepida, quamuis fremat horridus Orcus & Or- Namq; piis, Ioua, nil, prohibente, nocent. (bis:
Concipe spem firmam: Deus est qui corda bonorum Laudat, & iratus facta superba notat.
Ille Deus, Deus ille suum non deserit agmen: Iudicia hic iusto tempore iusta dabit.
Iniustos rebus uideas si forte secundis Elatos, nimioq; animum turgescere fastu: Ne tibi mens tristem mox efferuescat in iram.

Nam uelut herba uirens modo, post arescit, & o- Succisa subito amittit radice uigorem; Utq; per incultos marcescunt gramina campos Agricolæ desecta manu: sic tota malorum Successu defuncta breui mox turba peribit.
Quin potius confide Deo, uitijsq; relictis, Quæ bona sunt semper studio sectare fideli, Incola sic terræ secura pace frueris.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Profeßo" in the first line may be "Profiteor" or a variant; I read it as printed. "reliĉtis" carries a mark over the c, read here as "relictis". "efferuescat" is read as printed. The Latin couplets are split at the couplet level, so the stanza grouping is my judgement. The marginal "(mnem" beside the second stanza is partial and may be a fragment of a note or of a marginal mark. The stanza numbers "1", "2", "3" in the right margin are read from small glyphs and may be misread. Two small marks under the last line, to the right, could not be read and were not transcribed. The catchword "Nul" is cut off at the edge, so the completion is uncertain. The page number is printed as "361", with the final 1 partly worn. The running head is absent on this page.
